why: flatten(finalize = false) is public API that no test or caller uses; with the mutant it still finalizes commands, so a test calling flatten(false) and checking that parameters are unfinalized (value access throws) or that finalization errors are deferred would kill it.

Every caller passes an empty list when this is reached (ParserInternals and MutuallyExclusive pass emptyList(); CoOccurring short-circuits on invocationsByOption.isNotEmpty() before any non-empty list could be passed), so the removed early return is never taken.

Forcing minArgCount to 0 lets a token matching a subcommand name be taken as a subcommand even when a required argument is still unfilled (e.g. a command with a required argument and a subcommand 'sub', parsed with 'sub sub'), and no test uses an argument value that equals a subcommand name.
Treating every argument as optional makes minArgCount 0, so a required argument whose value equals a subcommand name (e.g. 'sub sub') gets parsed as a subcommand; no test covers this.

A required vararg (multiple(required=true), nvalues=-1) next to a required single argument would make the mutant's sum 0 instead of 1, so a leading token equal to a subcommand name becomes a subcommand; no test combines these.
